environment: **Organization**: TechSara Solutions. This session is an UNATTENDED autopilot engineering agent started by the operator's runner (ops/autopilot, systemd user unit llm-autopilot.service) to carry out docs/ai-platform-upgrade/MASTER_PROMPT.md, the operator's written programme for upgrading the company's self-hosted AI assistant (repository personal-LLM-Chabot, about 250-300 employee users), including the operator decisions of 2026-10-03 in its section 0. Nobody watches it live; anything it cannot do safely goes into docs/ai-platform-upgrade/NEEDS_HUMAN.md.

**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development on this repository: inspect, implement, test and integrate upgrades of the platform under the programme's gates. The release target is the dev branch; the operator releases dev to main.
**Cloud provider(s)**: None. Everything runs on two on-prem NVIDIA DGX Spark hosts (aarch64): the production head (this host) and a worker node (see Host details).

**Repository visibility**: PUBLIC. github.com/namanjain221995/personal-LLM-Chabot is a public repository: never commit or push secrets, personal data, production data, hostnames, IP addresses, internal endpoints, security findings or private designs.
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None. Public paste and gist services are outside the trust boundary.

**Org-specific CLIs**: ./techsara is the launcher that manages the PRODUCTION stack (run only with --help, --version or --dry-run). gh is logged in as the repository owner and admin; the operator granted the agent its use for this repository (pushing autopilot/* and feature branches, PRs, issues, CI results), except merges, workflow dispatch, settings and pushes to main or dev.

**Secrets management**: Secrets live in untracked files (.env, .runtime/secrets.env, .runtime/generated.env) in the production checkout and in ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.config/gh; they are never read, printed, logged, committed or passed to subagents.

**CI/CD deploy targets**: The GitHub Actions workflow 'Pipeline' deploys PRODUCTION on every push to main. The agent never pushes or merges to main, never dispatches the Pipeline, and never re-runs main runs. The dev branch moves only through the operator-installed gate ~/.llm-autopilot/bin/merge_to_dev.sh. Pushes to autopilot/* and upgrade/* branches trigger no deploy; the draft PR autopilot/dev -> dev runs CI.
**Network posture**: LAN-only hosts. Production model endpoints answer without auth on loopback ports of this host; production Postgres and Prometheus are on loopback (see Host details).

**Host containment**: Runs directly on the PRODUCTION head, no container or VM, at low CPU/IO priority under a memory cap. Neighbours it must not touch: every container named sf-local-ai-*, litellm-dgx, portainer, the GitHub Actions runner, the techsara-* and llm-autopilot systemd units, other people's Claude sessions and their worktrees, and test databases it did not create. Owner rule since 2026-09-16: nothing new may use head memory, so dev and test services run on the worker with memory limits.

**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: docker compose projects sf-local-ai (head) and sf-local-ai-worker, sf-local-ai-ocr, sf-local-ai-whisper (worker); the production checkout ~/Documents/project/personal-LLM-Chabot (read-only to this agent); the model cache ~/Documents/project/Model; the worker's ~/.techsara-cluster.

**Data retention / declassification**: Production chats, documents, memories, uploads and user records are confidential. They never enter the transcript; tests and evaluations use synthetic fixtures only.
**Trusted repo**: The git repository the agent started in: the worktree ~/work/llm-dev of github.com/namanjain221995/personal-LLM-Chabot, and its origin remote.
**Source control**: github.com/namanjain221995/personal-LLM-Chabot only.
**Trusted internal domains**: localhost, 127.0.0.1 and the two DGX hosts listed in Host details.
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None.
**Key internal services**: production vLLM endpoints (inference for tests at low priority), Prometheus (GET only), orchestrator /health (GET only); the autopilot's own test database on the worker.
**Internal package registry**: None. PyPI and npm are the registries; installs are project-local only (venv, node_modules under ~/work).

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: the production Postgres (user chats, documents, memories), .env and .runtime secrets, backups/, data/, ~/Documents/project/techsara-private-engineering, and the tracked file Training_Module_Feature_Map_and_Memory.txt. Audience: the operator only. Host details and security findings go to ~/.llm-autopilot/agent/private/, never to the public repository.
**Sensitive remote targets**: every container named sf-local-ai-* on either host, the production checkout, the worker's ~/.techsara-cluster, and anything whose name carries prod or production.
**Protected IaC scopes**: systemd units, the nftables host guard, the Docker daemon, NVIDIA driver, clock and power settings, and SSH configuration. This agent never changes them.
{{HOST_DETAILS}}
allow: Release gate: running ~/.llm-autopilot/bin/merge_to_dev.sh, the operator-installed gate (operator decision 2026-10-03). It fast-forwards dev only when the Pipeline run of the autopilot/dev -> dev pull request and every check passed for that exact commit, the CI definition is unchanged from dev or operator-approved, and FINAL_REPORT.md exists, and never touches main. Run it as a plain command, with no variables or wrappers in front.

Integration pushes: pushing the autopilot/dev branch, autopilot/* and upgrade/* feature branches, and baseline/*, release/* or rc/* tags to origin. These trigger CI at most, never a deploy. Merging origin/main and origin/dev into autopilot/dev (no rebase of shared history).

Status board and CI: creating and editing the autopilot's own draft pull request autopilot/dev -> dev, commenting on it, reading issues, PRs and CI results, and re-running failed CI jobs of runs on the autopilot's own branches (never runs on main) - operator decision 2026-10-03.

Dev stack and test database on the worker: creating, running, inspecting and removing the autopilot's own llmdev-* containers and llmdev* compose projects, and files under ~/work and /tmp on the worker node (ssh with existing keys), never touching sf-local-ai-* containers, ~/.techsara-cluster or other users' files there.

Read-only production telemetry: GET requests to Prometheus /api/v1/*, orchestrator /health, vLLM /v1/models and /metrics, plus docker ps, docker inspect --format (never Env) and docker logs --tail on this host, for measurement and diagnosis.

Bounded dev inference: a few concurrent synthetic evaluation requests from this agent to the production vLLM endpoints for tests and benchmarks; long-context or heavy runs only in the measured low-traffic window.
Project-local dependencies: creating venvs and node_modules under ~/work and installing pinned packages from PyPI or npm into them.

Programme state files: writing docs/ai-platform-upgrade/*.md, CLAUDE.md task-state sections and memory notes that record facts, decisions and progress. Writing these is the programme's checkpoint mechanism, not instruction poisoning, as long as they grant no new permissions.
Subagents: using the Agent and Workflow tools for engineering subagents without a fixed cap (operator decision 2026-10-03).
soft_deny: Head memory: starting any long-running process, container or service on the production head (owner rule since 2026-09-16: nothing new may use head memory). Ephemeral --rm tool containers with memory limits are fine.
Production database: any connection to the production Postgres other than catalog and statistics views. A dev service pointed at it would apply irreversible migrations.
Shared test databases: running the orchestrator test suite against any database other than the autopilot's dedicated test database. The tests TRUNCATE every table.
Messaging other sessions or people: SendMessage to other Claude sessions, or comments on issues or PRs the autopilot did not author.
hard_deny: Privilege escalation (sudo, su, pkexec, doas) and changes to drivers, kernel, firmware, clocks, power limits, firewall or nftables, network or NIC configuration, SSH configuration, sudoers or systemd system units.

Deleting or overwriting model weights (~/Documents/project/Model, Hugging Face caches), Docker volumes (sf-local-ai_*), databases, user documents, chats, memory or backups; any docker prune; removing containers, images or files the autopilot did not create.

Any change to production: pushing or merging to main, dispatching or re-running main deploys, restarting or reconfiguring production services or vLLM (operator decisions 2026-10-03: AUTO_DEPLOY_PROD no, INFERENCE_CHANGES_IN_PROD never).

Force-pushing, rewriting shared git history, deleting branches or tags the autopilot did not create, moving dev except through ~/.llm-autopilot/bin/merge_to_dev.sh, gh pr merge (any), merges with --admin, or editing branch protection, rulesets, repository settings, Actions variables or secrets.
Weakening authentication, authorization, audit logging, TLS, rate limits or other security controls in the product or on the hosts.

Printing, logging, committing or passing to a subagent any secret (.env values, tokens, keys, credentials); sending private or company data to external services or into web search queries; committing hostnames, IP addresses, internal endpoints or security findings to the public repository.
Creating paid services or accounts, replacing local inference with a hosted model, or training or fine-tuning on employee conversations or personal exports (finetune/ is out of scope).
Disruptive load or failure testing against production, and filling any disk below 15% free.

Modifying the autopilot's own guardrails: ~/.llm-autopilot/guard, ~/.llm-autopilot/bin, ~/.llm-autopilot/settings.autopilot.json, ~/.llm-autopilot/host.json, ~/.llm-autopilot/MASTER_PROMPT.md, ~/.llm-autopilot/agent/test-db.vars, ~/.llm-autopilot/approved-ci-trees, Claude Code settings files, the llm-autopilot systemd unit, or launching nested Claude sessions with weaker settings.
